title: Delegates and events — one screen
rememberThis: A delegate is a Common Language Runtime (CLR) type that holds a method with a compatible signature, including the return type.
Multicast invocation walks the list synchronously; one throw stops later handlers unless you iterate GetInvocationList yourself.
The event keyword is not a public delegate field: outsiders may += and -= only, never assign or invoke.
Lambdas capture unless marked static; captured locals become a closure that can pin the enclosing object.
C# 14 extension blocks add instance and static extension properties; they still lose to real instance members at bind time.
bullets: Prefer Func<T,TResult> and Action<T> over custom delegates unless the type name is part of a public contract.
Long-lived queue consumers that expose events must unsubscribe in Dispose; otherwise scoped subscribers leak.
Local functions can yield and avoid delegate allocation when called directly; lambdas cannot yield.
C# 14 lets lambda parameters take ref/in/out/scoped without spelling types; params still needs explicit types.
JavaScript functions are first-class objects; C# methods become values only when bound to a delegate.

rows.label: Func vs Action
rows.value: Func returns TResult; Action returns void. Predicate<T> is Func<T,bool> with a name.

rows.label: Multicast +
rows.value: Combining two delegates builds a new invocation list. -= removes the last matching entry.

rows.label: static lambda
rows.value: Cannot capture locals, parameters, or instance state. Use on hot paths to prove no closure.

rows.label: event vs delegate
rows.value: Public EventHandler field: anyone can null or invoke. event: add/remove only from outside.

rows.label: C# 14 extension
rows.value: extension(T receiver) { ... } inside a static class; static extension(T) for type-level members.

rows.label: JS EventTarget
rows.value: Same function reference to remove; C# -= same delegate instance. Both can leak if emitter outlives listener.
